rationale: THE EXTERNAL SINGLE-TYPE-IMPORT BINDING CLAIM — THE INDEXED HALF (java lane, 2026-10-20). This fixture lives in a sub-directory, so the runner gives it a real project index (JAVA_DECLARATION_SPEC, complete=true): the lane's rules are fail-closed without a COMPLETE key space, because a tie is a fact about the PROJECT. POSITIVE: `import com.vendor.ext.Tool;` binds the simple name `Tool`, and the project declares `Tool` in TWO places (ToolOwners.Tool and ToolOwners.Other.Tool), so the name-keyed resolver TIES on the name — a WALL. The imported type is outside the project (the index does not declare `com.vendor.ext.Tool`) and inside this file the import decides which `Tool` the name means (JLS 6.4.1). The import edge publishes the EVIDENCE the arbiter verifies the claim against (metadata.importedBindings + metadata.module) and the type-position edge whose target is the bound name publishes the CLAIM. NEGATIVES: (1) `com.vendor.ext.Unique` — the project declares `Unique` ONCE, so the name model RESOLVES that row and a claim there would trade a resolution for a claim: neither evidence nor claim; (2) `singleimportproject.Own` — the project owns the type, so the import is project code and must resolve through the owner/name model; (3) `Tool.make()` — a CALL whose target is a member leaf, not the bound name.
